Use the best model for the job.

No single model is best at everything. One paints, one writes code, one reads what it sees. Your coworker switches mid-thread, on your own plan or an API key, and keeps the same chat, files and computer. Each reply says which one answered and who paid.

Allowly · Mac

You tap Allow. It actually presses Allow.

A tool for working with agents. Your coworker hits a macOS permission prompt while you're out, and it lands on your phone. Tap the answer: a USB board on your Mac clicks it like a real mouse, and types like a real keyboard.

AutomationGatekeeperAccessibilityTrackpadPasswordFull Disk AccessAll clear

Modal promptmacOS asks in a dialogAutomation, Files & Folders, Camera, a newly downloaded app. Tap the answer on the phone; the board clicks it.
Manual toggleOnly System Settings can grant itAccessibility, Screen Recording. Your phone becomes a trackpad to click the switch, then a keyboard for the Mac password.
Manual addThe app isn't in the list yetFull Disk Access. The board clicks +, picks the app in the Finder sheet, then turns it on.
Egress

Your IP, not a datacenter's.

Sites trust a home connection and question a datacenter. Route your coworker's computer through your own desktop, and its logins look like you at your desk: no new-location checks, no phone approvals.
